headline: Leafs’ Sissons exits game due to lower-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Toronto forward Colton Sissons left Sunday's game against the Devils with a lower-body injury, and notes that it isn't quite clear what led to him not returning.

The injury lands on a Leafs team that is 8-9-2 and sitting at 18 points through 19 games. Our numbers suggest the record may be flattering them a little. Toronto's share of expected goals (a measure of chance quality, where 50% is an even split) is 47.1% so far this season, and it is 46% at five-on-five. The Leafs have also scored 6.5 more goals than their chances would predict, so some of their results are leaning on finishing that may not last. New Jersey, at 13-5-0, was the stronger side on the ice, with a 59.2% expected goal share. Losing a depth forward matters less than those underlying numbers, but a team already being outplayed has little room to absorb another absence. We don't have a breakdown of who picks up Sissons' minutes, so we'll wait for word on the severity before saying where the ice time goes.
